description: Phone screenshot of a tweet (author handle cropped out of frame) commenting on the August 2018 arrest of a man before a Trump rally in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania. The tweet includes a photograph of a Press Enterprise newspaper front page dated Thursday, August 2, 2018, headlined 'TRUMP ATTACK FOILED', reporting that Jeffrey Gardner Boyd, 55, of Tulsa, Oklahoma was arrested in Briar Creek, PA with a loaded pistol after allegedly threatening President Trump and his family; the article says an unidentified local woman he had met on Twitter alerted police. The tweet's author implies she is the 'Mystery Woman' referenced in the article.
text: This "Mystery Woman" would really like to hug OUR FAVORITE PRESIDENT. I'm sure @SecretService would have stopped this guy too but I'm glad I got him off the streets before you arrived. See article below ~ Part 2 next tweet. Beattie, Hubberd and McDermott Obituaries Page 4. Thursday, August 2, 2018. $1. TRUMP ATTACK FOILED. Oklahoma man drove here with loaded gun, police say. By LEON BOGDAN Press Enterprise Writer. BRIAR CREEK - An Oklahoma man was arrested here and is being held in lieu of $1 million bail for allegedly threatening to assassinate President Donald Trump and his family. He was taken into custody and his weapon confiscated Tuesday after he had driven here nonstop to meet a local woman with whom he had discussed politics on Twitter, arrest papers say. Trump is scheduled to appear at a rally this evening in Wilkes-Barre. Alerted by the woman of the threat to the president, State Police began searching for Jeffrey Gardner Boyd, 55, of Tulsa. Troopers from the Shickshinny barracks found him Tuesday afternoon, parked at the Giant Foods store. Inside his vehicle they found a loaded Springfield .45-caliber pistol and two extra magazines, both full, police said. Mystery woman. Boyd is reported to have said that he drove nonstop from Oklahoma to Columbia County to meet the woman. She is a Trump supporter and had posted pro-Trump remarks, which he had been following on her Twitter account in recent days, arrest papers say. Police did not publicly identify the woman. She told authorities that Boyd told her he feared she "may be in danger." Boyd also told her the CIA was "sending messages directly into his head," and that he was hearing "voices" telling him to kill Trump as well as Donald Trump Jr., Ivanka Trump and her husband, Jared Kushner.
